title: [Mouse Without Borders] Input events arrive out of order: two concurrent MainTCPRoutine threads inject via SendInput without ordering guarantees
summary: Preserve the ordered-input and injection-failure-containment directions, but incorporate the new selective mitigation: the receiver's 50-ID duplicate history can forget a delayed copy. Two-stream ordering and duplicate retention are related but distinct; enlarging the array or adding a lock alone is not a complete reliability fix.

next_action.label: Test delayed duplicate packets and input recovery
next_action.reason: No duplicate input, reordered transitions or connection teardown from an isolated recoverable injection failure.

judgment.rationale: Preserve the ordered-input and injection-failure-containment directions, but incorporate the new selective mitigation: the receiver's 50-ID duplicate history can forget a delayed copy. Two-stream ordering and duplicate retention are related but distinct; enlarging the array or adding a lock alone is not a complete reliability fix.
evidence: Original 0.101.2362 two-machine report supplies typing transpositions and a one-socket diagnostic control, not a recommendation to change the firewall permanently.
The November 16 0.102.3101 test reproduces extra injected mouse buttons with service mode off and one elevated interactive MWB process.
Changing only the receiver history from 50 to 8192 removed extra clicks in the follow-up capture, but one earlier click was absent; packet IDs were not captured.
The original report separately supplies SendInputEx 0x8007007A exceptions followed by reconnection.

Current Common.SkSend assigns one packet ID then sends it through each eligible peer connection: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/82bd57f5d23ee19a98b0c46f42c304742a7db426/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Common.cs

Receiver.PreProcess retains only 50 IDs under a lock; ProcessPackage dispatches after that dedup boundary: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/82bd57f5d23ee19a98b0c46f42c304742a7db426/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Receiver.cs

MainTCPRoutine closes the current socket when packet-processing exceptions escape: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/82bd57f5d23ee19a98b0c46f42c304742a7db426/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/SocketStuff.cs
New capture/mutation result and its explicit limitations: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/51328#issuecomment-6913043163
judgment.recommended_action: No duplicate input, reordered transitions or connection teardown from an isolated recoverable injection failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: Conditional lightweight direction; Preserve the ordered-input and injection-failure-containment directions, but incorporate the new selective mitigation: the receiver's 50-ID duplicate history can forget a delayed copy. Two-stream ordering and duplicate retention are related but distinct; enlarging the array or adding a lock alone is not a complete reliability fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Define one peer/session-scoped input sequencing and duplicate-acceptance boundary rather than a global tiny recent-ID list.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Source proves a finite arrival-count duplicate window and multi-connection dispatch; delayed-copy acceptance fits the selective result, but exact in-flight ID timing and the original keyboard-order mechanism remain inferred.
plan: Define one peer/session-scoped input sequencing and duplicate-acceptance boundary rather than a global tiny recent-ID list.

Align sequence assignment with send order and serialize ordered receiver injection; explicitly handle delayed copies, session reset, wrap and gaps without silently discarding required key/button releases.
Keep a larger bounded history only as a measured mitigation, not proof of ordering or losslessness.
Preserve the separate packet-level injection-exception containment change and regression tests.
verification: After more than 50 intervening packets, replaying an old packet through the second connection does not inject it twice.
Interleaved two-stream key/button down/move/up order, reconnects and session resets leave no stuck input.
Two-machine capture compares physical versus injected events without typed content and does not infer network latency from unsynchronized clocks.

confidence.rationale: Source proves a finite arrival-count duplicate window and multi-connection dispatch; delayed-copy acceptance fits the selective result, but exact in-flight ID timing and the original keyboard-order mechanism remain inferred.

proposed_fixes.title: Contain individual injection failures without silently losing held-input state
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The reported SendInputEx exception can escape into MainTCPRoutine's socket-closing catch; this containment issue does not explain or fix the underlying insufficient-buffer error.
plan: Catch injection errors at the input-packet boundary with bounded diagnostics.
Recover any partially applied modifier/button state safely, and keep subsequent packet reception active.
Investigate the originating SendInput failure independently of transport lifetime.
verification: An injected failure does not close the socket or prevent the next valid packet.
Partial-input recovery leaves no stuck key/button and does not mask persistent transport failure.

confidence.rationale: The supplied stack/reconnect evidence matches the current enclosing receive-loop catch; containment remains distinct from the original injection defect.

actions.label: Approve MWB ordering and injection-recovery design
Test delayed duplicate packets and input recovery

reproduce.title: Verify Mouse Without Borders report
prerequisites: Mouse Without Borders enabled where applicable
setup: Two owned PCs with ordinary firewall configuration and both eligible peer connections retained.
Use synthetic input/packet fixtures; any physical capture records only button/modifier metadata, not typed content.
steps: 1. Send an input packet, process over 50 distinct subsequent IDs, then deliver its delayed duplicate on the second connection.
2. Interleave key/button release sequences and verify dedup plus injection order.
3. Force one SendInput failure and verify later packets remain receivable without stale held state.
reproduce.expected_result: No duplicate input, reordered transitions or connection teardown from an isolated recoverable injection failure.
